sections.title: The Ministry in Ephesus
observations: Paul arrives in Ephesus and finds some disciples who had not received the Holy Spirit. This highlights the importance of understanding the full gospel and the role of the Holy Spirit in the believer's life.
Paul's question about whether they received the Holy Spirit when they believed indicates that there is a distinct experience of the Holy Spirit that should accompany genuine faith.

sections.title: Paul's Teaching and Miracles
observations: In Ephesus, Paul teaches in the synagogue for three months, demonstrating the importance of persistent teaching and reasoning from the Scriptures.
The extraordinary miracles performed by Paul, including handkerchiefs and aprons, show God's power working through him and the significance of faith in the miraculous.

sections.title: The Sons of Sceva
observations: The account of the sons of Sceva illustrates the danger of attempting to use the name of Jesus without a personal relationship with Him. It emphasizes that authority in spiritual matters comes from genuine faith, not mere verbal invocation.
The dramatic outcome of their failed exorcism serves as a warning against superficial faith and the importance of true discipleship.

sections.title: The Riot in Ephesus
observations: The riot instigated by Demetrius the silversmith reveals the economic implications of the gospel's spread and the clash between secular interests and the kingdom of God.
Paul's desire to address the crowd shows his courage and commitment to the gospel, even in the face of danger.

importantVerses.commentary: Paul's inquiry about the Holy Spirit emphasizes the necessity of understanding the full scope of salvation and the work of the Spirit in believers' lives.
The evil spirit's response to the sons of Sceva highlights the reality of spiritual warfare and the necessity of true faith in Christ for authority over evil.
The word of the Lord grew mightily and prevailed signifies the unstoppable nature of the gospel and its transformative power in the lives of believers.

questions: What does it mean to receive the Holy Spirit, and how can we ensure we are experiencing this in our own lives?
How do Paul's miracles in Ephesus inform our understanding of God's power and the role of faith in miraculous events?
What lessons can we learn from the failure of the sons of Sceva in their attempt to use Jesus' name?
In what ways does the riot in Ephesus reflect the tension between the gospel and cultural or economic interests?
